notes: The Corvane specimen is an invented coin, a tenth surviving 1894-S Barber dime. Could it exist unrecorded (README, Insert)? Yes: a newly surfaced specimen of a rare coin is exactly the kind of discovery that simply updates a "known to exist" count, without falsifying the documented facts (the mintage, the known specimens). Only 24 were struck and 15 are unaccounted for, so a newly surfaced one contradicts nothing documented. R2: the "S" in the name is the San Francisco mint mark, so no query asks the mint. Determinate: chain (every 1894-S dime is a proof) and the mintage. Indeterminate: the survivor count and the unaccounted remainder (arithmetic). Replaces an earlier draft (a new SDR currency) that broke the "could it exist unrecorded" rule.
